issue_snapshot.title: Follow-ups from #60: 1 from the review
issue_snapshot.body:
What the review and QA of PR #61 (for #60) found and did not fix there — filed as it merged, one ticket for the lot.

## From the review

Non-blocking findings the reviewer approved despite: a statement about severity, not a judgement that they are wrong.

### The added JSX comment is two lines and also describes the amount span from a position above the name span; the repo's guidance is one short line, and the test header already carries the same explanation.

> The added JSX comment is two lines and also describes the amount span from a position above the name span; the repo's guidance is one short line, and the test header already carries the same explanation.
> 
> `app/groups/[id]/page.tsx:547`
> 
> Evidence: gh pr diff 61 adds a two-line {/* min-w-0: ... ml-auto on the amount ... */} block between the li and the outer span.
> 
> Fix: Trim to one line ("min-w-0: overflow-wrap cannot lower a flex item's min-content floor.") or drop it in favour of the test header.

---

**Check each one still reproduces before planning it.** They were written against the PR as it stood, and a later round can have fixed one. Some may not hold up: say so and drop them rather than implementing something that was never wrong. Split this if they turn out to be unrelated.

Depends on #60.

validated_work_order.understanding: The one review finding from PR #61 still holds on main: app/groups/[id]/page.tsx:547-548 carries a two-line JSX comment between the transfer <li> and its outer name <span>. It explains min-w-0 on the name span and also describes ml-auto on the amount span, which sits further down, not at this position. Repo guidance is one short line, and app/groups/[id]/transfer-line-wrap.test.ts (header, lines 8-11) already explains both min-w-0 and ml-auto. This is a comment-only trim; rendered markup is unchanged.
validated_work_order.approach: Replace the two-line comment with the reviewer's suggested single line: {/* min-w-0: overflow-wrap cannot lower a flex item's min-content floor. */}, same indentation, leaving the markup beneath it untouched. The ml-auto half is dropped because it describes a different element and the test header carries it (and a test pins the ml-auto class). The new line must not contain the literal strings '<span', '{transferWords(' or 'data-amount', which transfer-line-wrap.test.ts and amounts-tabular.test.ts locate by indexOf/lastIndexOf; the suggested text contains none. No test change is needed. Do not touch the other multi-line JSX comments in this block (:538-541, :555-556): the issue names only :547.

files.change: Lines 547-548: replace the two-line JSX comment with the single line {/* min-w-0: overflow-wrap cannot lower a flex item's min-content floor. */}; keep it a JSX child comment inside the <li>, and leave the <span className="flex min-w-0 flex-wrap items-baseline gap-2"> that follows unchanged.
files.why: Resolves the review finding: guidance is one short line, and the amount's ml-auto is already explained in the test header.

acceptance.check: The JSX comment above the transfer line's outer name wrapper in app/groups/[id]/page.tsx is a single line and no longer mentions ml-auto or the amount.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Read the diff of app/groups/[id]/page.tsx: two comment lines become one, nothing else changes. This is judged from the diff (no test asserts comment wording).

acceptance.check: The transfer line's rendered classes are unchanged: transfer-line-wrap.test.ts and amounts-tabular.test.ts still pass, and typecheck and build are green.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Run npx vitest run app/groups/[id]/transfer-line-wrap.test.ts, then the sdlc:verify suite (typecheck + test:ci + build).

qa_script: Open app/groups/[id]/page.tsx at the transfer list and confirm the comment is one line and the markup beneath it is unchanged.
Run the transfer-line-wrap test and the verify suite; all pass.

alternatives_considered.approach: Delete the comment entirely and rely on the test header.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The min-w-0 rationale is non-obvious next to break-words and a reader would likely strip it; the reviewer's first-named fix keeps one short line on the spot.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep both facts in one long line.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Still describes the amount span from the wrong position, which is the second half of the finding.

alternatives_considered.approach: Also shorten the neighbouring multi-line comments at :538-541 and :555-556.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Not in the issue; they carry a real ADR-linked rationale and widening a chore is scope creep.

assumptions: No test reads the comment text; both tests that scan this region (transfer-line-wrap.test.ts, amounts-tabular.test.ts) anchor on '<span', '{transferWords(' and 'data-amount', which the new comment does not contain.
risks: .sdlc/memory/conventions.md quotes the same min-content-floor sentence; it is the Librarian's and no ticket may change it, so it is left alone.
out_of_scope: Any change to the transfer line's classes or layout.
Other multi-line JSX comments in page.tsx (:538-541, :555-556).
validated_work_order.confidence_rationale: One finding, reproduced by reading the current file; a comment-only edit whose only textual readers (two source-assertion tests) I read and which cannot collide with the one-line text. Would drop only if the implementer retyped the comment with a literal '<span' or 'data-amount'.
evidence: app/groups/[id]/page.tsx:547-548 is the two-line comment on main (HEAD 6c7bda0); ml-auto sits on the amount span at ~:566.
app/groups/[id]/transfer-line-wrap.test.ts:8-11 already explains min-w-0 and ml-auto; line 63 pins ml-auto on the amount span's classes, so the class is protected without the comment.
transfer-line-wrap.test.ts only reads this region via indexOf('{transferWords(') / indexOf('data-amount') / lastIndexOf('<span'); the new comment contains none.
validated_work_order.debate_summary: The critique returned 'sound' with three minor findings and no blocking ones; I agreed with the proposal's diagnosis after reading page.tsx and the test myself. Finding 1 (AC-1 labelled 'test' though no test asserts the comment): accepted in substance — kept the verify label required by the schema but reworded how_to_verify to say it is judged from the diff; no test for comment wording, which would be over-engineering. Finding 2 (neighbouring comments at :538-541 and :555-556 are also multi-line, so 'one-line rule' is not what the file does): accepted as a scope note, not acted on; the issue names only :547, so they stay and the PR must not claim the file is now one-line throughout. Finding 3 (ml-auto left without a comment at its use site): dismissed as a defect — the issue asks for exactly this and the test pinning ml-auto protects it. The critique's missed edge cases (anchor strings, must remain a JSX child comment, ~94-column line) are folded into the approach; the width is not a failure since the repo has no lint/format script. No real disagreement between proposer and critic.
residual_risks: AC-1 is judged from the diff only; nothing will fail if the comment is later re-expanded.
Other multi-line JSX comments in this block remain by design.
